h: A Fife Day Out Built Around the Deer
p: Deer are surprisingly varied once you start looking closely. Some are big and stately, others small and dainty, with different coats, antlers and behaviours, and spotting the differences is a great game for younger visitors. Autumn is a particularly atmospheric time to come, as it's the rutting season, when stags get noisy and show off. If you're after photos, the softer light of morning or late afternoon makes all the difference.

Practical bits: wear boots or trainers you don't mind getting muddy, as some of the paths can be soggy after Scottish rain. Pack a waterproof even on a bright morning, because the weather in Fife can change quickly. There's usually a café and shop on site for a warming drink when you're done.

Make a proper Fife day of it. Hill of Tarvit, a lovely Edwardian mansion run by the National Trust for Scotland, sits just outside Cupar, with gardens and woodland walks of its own. A short drive west brings you to Falkland, a gorgeous little village with its historic royal palace, once a favourite retreat of the Stuart kings and queens, including Mary, Queen of Scots.

For a breath of sea air, Tentsmuir Forest on the coast north of St Andrews has pine woodland trails leading to a wide sandy beach, and you might well spot seals hauled out on the sandbanks nearby. Cupar has its own railway station on the line between Edinburgh and Dundee, so it's also an easy base for exploring further afield without the car.
